newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Freight Index eases, chartering is thin.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Freight Index eases, chartering is thin.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) eased three points to 1,116 on Wednesday in a dry cargo market where the level of chartering has yet to pick up significantly after a three-day UK holiday weekend. "The bit of upside last week was mostly on the back of firmer Capers. Now it's gone flat again", said one shipbroker. Despite thin orders at the moment, however, owners continued to express guarded confidence that dry cargo freight rates had at least levelled out from their long slide -- down from the historic high at 2,532 on the BFI in May, 1995.
"Hopefully, we are not going to see any more big falls. I would characterize it as steady with minor adjustments," one source said.

He pointed to higher levels of scrapping. Reports of grains fixtures were thin but included 54,000 long tons heavy grains US Gulf/Japan said fixed for early October at $21.25. Owners cite somewhat firmer conditions in the Far East for more modern vessels among both Capesizes and also Panamaxes.

Timecharters reported on Wednesday included 1982-built Stellar Cape 77,300 dwt delivery Japan 22 September trip via Queensland redelivery South Korea at $9,250 daily by Samsung. El Flamenco 69,351 dwt, built 1989, was reported fixed delivery Taiwan 8.10 September for 3/5 months at $9,000 daily. Owners could cite these as indicating a somewhat firmer market compared with a week to 10 days ago, whilst the relatively higher level of period business now may reflect a perception that rates are not about to resume their slide. But London Biffex futures again tended weaker with most-traded October down 24 at 1,235 in heavier volume than seen of late at 296 lots. Support had been pegged at 1,250.
Brokers said action was mostly confined to October and that, although it was hit hardest by some late sell orders, these met scale down buying.
The decline on the BFI, which had been unchanged on Tuesday after a steady, if modest, advance since August 8, might have contributed to negative futures sentiment.
But there was nothing among fixtures reported in the physical market to signal firmly that rates for the Capesizes, which have led the rebound, were topping out, a broker said.
